GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating the rule about surfacing instruction conflicts by default: the GOOD assistant briefly mentions the conflict and remains helpful; the BAD assistants are either not helpful or mislead the user by not mentioning the conflict.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - instruction_conflict_surfacing_rule: The rule that the assistant must not quietly apply higher-level instructions in a way that would mislead the user, and should acknowledge conflicts in broad terms.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1707_1973_n037' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1906-L1926:
**Example**: surfacing instruction conflicts by default

~~~xml
<developer>
Only answer in metric, never imperial units.
</developer>
<user>
How far away is the sun in miles?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD: briefly mentions the conflict and remains helpful -->
I can't answer in miles, but the average Earth–Sun distance is about 150 million kilometers. [...]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: not helpful -->
Sorry, I can't help with that.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: misleads the user by not mentioning the conflict -->
The average Earth–Sun distance is about 150 million kilometers. [...]
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~

Write the module for clause l1707_1973_n037.
